system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s draft is not a balanced package from the Buyer’s perspective. I would reject blanket limitations and general disclosure, and make Completion protection depend on resolving or expressly pricing the identified risks. This is a negotiation review, not a substitute for advice on the full SPA and due diligence record.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **AUD 4.8m (20% of price)**. | A materially higher cap, sized to the diligence and risk profile; separate caps for specific indemnities and other claim categories. | **Seek a higher general cap and separate indemnity caps**—20% may not cover material warranty exposure. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower or no de minimis, and a smaller tipping basket (or a deductible basket where recovery starts only above the threshold); carve out fundamental, tax and specific indemnity claims. | **Reduce thresholds and exclude protected claim categories**—the proposed filters can leave meaningful aggregate loss unrecovered. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; proposes all Claims follow any applicable limit unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty period (at least 24 months as a starting position), with distinct periods for tax, title/fundamental and specific indemnity claims, and claim-preservation mechanics. | **Reject an 18-month catch-all**—it risks time-barring claims before relevant issues can be identified or assessed. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped protection for title and capacity, with a longer period; no general basket or de minimis. | **Carve out title and capacity from the general regime**—a 100% share acquisition depends on valid ownership and authority. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Express carve-outs for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including appropriate attribution rules), from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the extent legally permitted. | **Require an express fraud carve-out**—otherwise the limitation package may be argued to restrict remedies for deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of all indexed data-room contents, Accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure by reference**—it can qualify warranties for matters not fairly brought to the Buyer’s attention. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | No broad imputed or constructive knowledge bar; if agreed at all, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable enquiry, with appropriate carve-outs. | **Delete the proposed qualifier**—mere discoverability should not transfer the Seller’s warranty risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows about 30% of FY26 revenue and the letter says final consent and evidence of conditions are absent. | A condition precedent requiring final, unconditional consent and satisfaction/waiver of clause 11.3 conditions before Completion, with termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make compliant consent a Completion condition**—Bluefen’s revenue concentration and missing conditions evidence make post-Completion uncertainty material. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms no repayment or final security discharge is in the data room. | Repay and discharge at or before Completion, with lender release evidence and closing funds-flow mechanics; no reliance on a post-Completion promise. | **Require repayment and release at Completion**—a later release leaves the Company and Buyer exposed to continuing debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are not separately itemised in the draft funds flow and are described as the Seller’s matter. | Confirm entitlement, conditions, payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs; include all amounts in the completion debt/leakage or price adjustment mechanics, or require Seller funding. | **Reconcile and fund the full cost in the funds flow**—the disclosed bonuses are conditional liabilities omitted from it, with on-costs unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 says transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering the cost of securing, replacing or defending the required IP rights and resulting loss, backed by payment and assignment evidence; separately capped and timed. | **Expand the protection and require proof of transfer**—an indemnity limited to payment does not secure the Project Materials or address broader title risk. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 is described as preliminary and not expected to be material; Seller says no confirmed breach or loss. | Preserve claims and disclosure; require prompt full investigation, incident records, remediation and any legally required notification, with a specific indemnity or tailored protection for resulting liability and costs. | **Do not dismiss or waive the risk as immaterial**—scope, access and notification remain unresolved for a potentially sensitive 1,240 records. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 total) treated as ordinary-course costs. | Establish timing, scope, whether binding/terminable and accrued, and whether any amount is unpaid or outside the agreed price mechanics; obtain any needed termination or adjustment protection. | **Verify and quantify before Completion**—the disclosure does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; tax/IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, with tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies; clarify interaction with debt-free/cash-free price mechanics. | **Reject a single regime for all claims**—different risks need distinct protection, and the Seller’s catch-all could erode negotiated remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100% of issued shares. | Independently verify the register, issued capital, encumbrances and any relevant corporate records; obtain proper transfer instruments and closing deliverables, with title warranties. | **Do not treat the register as conclusive diligence**—it is the stated source, not evidence that the Buyer has completed verification. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP settled under the general regime; no separate terms are provided. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranties/indemnities, defined scope, caps and survival periods, and confirm the IP chain of title and any needed assignments. | **Keep these items open pending agreed drafting and diligence**—the Seller’s assertion does not resolve their scope or allocate their risks. |
=== END ADVICE ===
